subject.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap

question: Should OpenShell retain the proposed explicit 100 MiB compatibility-oriented cap, or adopt fs-safe's stricter 16 MiB default when moving to the bounded `root.read` path?
rationale: The cap is a user-visible sandbox read limit, so choosing it balances memory protection against compatibility for existing large-file workflows.

options.title: Keep an explicit 100 MiB cap
options.body: Use `root.read` with `maxBytes: 100 * 1024 * 1024` to preserve the PR's intended threshold while enforcing it in the supported safe primitive.

options.title: Adopt the fs-safe default
options.body: Rely on the default 16 MiB maximum for tighter resource protection, accepting that more existing sandbox reads will be rejected.

recommendation.title: Keep an explicit 100 MiB cap
recommendation.body: Use `root.read` with `maxBytes: 100 * 1024 * 1024` to preserve the PR's intended threshold while enforcing it in the supported safe primitive.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current pinned-read boundary that this change must preserve while adding a size policy.
